content: Diabetic kidney disease is diagnosed clinically based on the presence of albuminuria (elevated levels of albumin in the urine) and/or a reduced estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), even in the absence of other signs of kidney damage. This condition is most commonly observed in individuals with a long-standing history of diabetes, diabetic retinopathy, or a progressively declining eGFR over time. For an accurate diagnosis, it is recommended to measure the urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR) and eGFR. These measurements should take into account adjustments for racial and socioeconomic factors, as outlined by the Chronic Kidney Disease Epidemiology Collaboration (CKD-EPI) equation.
